data.name: Parmish
data.gender_notes: Parmish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit roots ‘par’ meaning supreme and ‘mishra’ meaning mixture, Parmish signifies the supreme lord or the one who is above all. In Hindu mythology, Parmish is a name given to various gods and goddesses, representing their supreme power and dominance. The name Parmish carries the meaning “Supreme Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parmish usually hope their child will grow to embody supreme lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the connection to the divine and the supreme power of the universe.
data.etymology: Parmish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Supreme Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parmish total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
